AtlasCom to share 10k anonymized chat examples and SLA requirements by 2027-11-29
Schedule on-prem deployment feasibility session w/ infra (private) week of 2027-12-06
Redwood to provide rough pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private by 2027-12-03
action_items: Ava Nguyen - Send data upload instructions + security questionnaire - 2027-11-27

summary: Discovery/POC scoping with AtlasCom focused on building a multilingual customer support routing and intent pipeline. Primary goals: select open models for classification + embeddings, define workload sizing and P99 latency targets, and determine deployment mode given EU data residency needs. Agreed next steps include Redwood running a 3-model benchmark on customer samples, AtlasCom to share data, and a follow-up infra feasibility meeting for private deployment.
topics: Success criteria: accuracy thresholds, routing latency, throughput
Workload sizing: daily volume, peak rate, concurrency
Deployment: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/onprem)
header:
Date: 2027-11-25
Time: 15:30 - 16:12 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Ava Nguyen (Redwood AE), Marcus Hill (Redwood SE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Moreno (AtlasCom PM), Rajiv Singh (AtlasCom Head of ML), Elena Petrova (AtlasCom Security), Tom Bates (AtlasCom SRE)
transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Lina - AtlasCom PM: Hi, Lina here. leading product for our customer ops AI, we want to reduce routing time and auto-triage in 4 languages to start (EN, ES, FR, DE).
[00:22] Marcus (Redwood SE): Marcus here, I'll drive the benchmarking and technical bits. quick note, we'll assume open models for cost control unless you prefer hosted proprietary.
[00:35] Rajiv - AtlasCom: We prefer open-models for auditability and cost. but we need EU data residency for EU customers, that's non-negotiable.
[00:46] Ava: got it. so high level success criteria? Lina, Rajiv?
[00:50] Lina: accuracy for intent classification needs to be > 92% on our top 10 intents, fallback to human if confidence < 0.6. routing latency ideally under 300ms p99 for classification, embeddings/search can be a bit higher but prefer < 800ms.
[01:10] Tom (SRE): throughput: about 50k messages/day currently, peaks up to 300 messages/min during events, concurrency maybe 40-50 simultaneous requests.
[01:26] Marcus: ok that helps with batching/throughput planning. do you have language distribution?
[01:30] Rajiv: roughly 65% EN, 18% ES, 10% FR, 7% DE. we also have some NL/IT but that's later.
[01:38] Sofia (Redwood SE): for multilingual quality we'll want to include per-lang eval sets, and separate fuzz tests for short terse messages vs long complaint threads.
[01:50] Elena (Security): security questions up front: are you offering Private deployment? we can't send EU PII outside EU. we need KMS integration, SOC2 plus iso, audit logs.
[02:02] Ava: we have Redwood Private options (VPC & onprem). we'll include security docs. Marcus will handle infra feasibility.
[02:12] Lina: Great. On model selection — we want a shortlist of open models balancing multilingual comprehension and inference cost. any suggestions?
[02:20] Marcus: Preliminary shortlist based on similar customers: OpenAssistant-Orchid-7b-multi, Llama-3-8b-quant variant, Mistral-13b-instruct (quant/qat), and a mid-tier 12b variant we sometimes call "ozone-12b" in our internal perf notes. we'll test both classification accuracy and embeddings quality for reranking.
[02:45] Rajiv: are there significant tradeoffs? e.g., Mistral 13b might be better quality but more expensive in dedicated capacity?
[02:53] Marcus: correct. 13b generally higher NLU quality for longer context and multilingual nuances but needs more memory, could push you from cheaper shared instance into reserved capacity. Llama-3-8b quant gives a good cost/latency sweet spot for classification. Orchid-7b is optimized for instruction-following in several languages but embeddings may lag native embedding models.
[03:14] Lina: embeddings - we plan to use semantic search for recent ticket retrieval and vector-based routing. we need to know if the same model can handle both classification and embeddings, or if separate embedding model is recommended.
[03:26] Marcus: recommended: use a small, fast embedding model for vector search (we can recommend a 2-4GB footprint quant model) and a separate classification model. Using the same LLM for both is possible but usually costs more and increases tail latency.
[03:38] Tom: about latency - you mentioned batching and continuous batching, what would that mean for our p99 300ms goal?
[03:45] Marcus: continuous batching helps throughput but adds decision latency if you wait too long. for classification we can set small max batch windows (e.g., 10-20ms) and prioritize low-latency path; for embeddings we'll do larger batches during non-peak or async flows. we'll tune to hit your p99 target.
[04:02] Elena: audit logs — we need detailed per-request tracing and token-level cost breakdowns for billing and compliance.
[04:10] Ava: Redwood Console provides per-route traces and token cost. we'll include an example export.
[04:16] Lina: timeline — we'd like a 6-week pilot: week 1 data exchange and bench plan, week 2-3 benchmarks, week 4 integration with test harness, week 5 live shadow traffic, week 6 evaluation + decision. possible?
[04:28] Marcus: that's tight but doable if data arrives on time. the big dependency is your infra sign-off for private deployment if we go that route.
[04:36] Rajiv: for benchmarks, what metrics will you run?
[04:40] Marcus: we'll run per-lang intent F1 and accuracy, confusion matrices for top intents, embedding recall@k for retrieval, latency p50/p95/p99, throughput sustained and peak, and CPU/GPU memory utilization. we'll also run adversarial tests — short-utterance vs slang vs code-switching.
[05:00] Lina: can you simulate our peaks? we can share traffic profiles.
[05:03] Marcus: yes we'll run synthetic load following your profile and also replay a de-identified portion of real traffic.
[05:10] Elena: encryption at rest + KMS? and do you support HSM for key custody?
[05:14] Ava: we support envelope encryption with KMS integrations; HSM options are part of the Private enterprise package. we'll add that to the security doc pack.
[05:23] Tom: operationally, what's the difference between Dedicated and Private for us?
[05:27] Sofia: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in Redwood infra with isolation and SLA; Private is customer-managed control plane (VPC or on-prem) for stricter data residency and network controls. Dedicated may be quicker to stand up but Private is needed if data can't leave their VPC.
[05:45] Rajiv: cost ballpark? we need rough hosted vs dedicated vs private to judge ROI before the pilot.
[05:50] Ava: we'll provide a ballpark based on throughput and model choices. Marcus will include estimates in the bench plan doc.
[06:00] Lina: model shortlist priorities: 1) hits multilingual F1 target, 2) meets p99 latency, 3) cost within budget.
[06:08] Marcus: noted. for the bench we'll include 3-model test: Orchid-7b-multi (fast), Llama-3-8b-quant (balance), Mistral-13b-instruct-qat (quality). plus a small embedding-only model for retrieval.
[06:24] Rajiv: any blockers on our side besides data? legal?
[06:28] Elena: we'll need to review DPA and run a security questionnaire; also need the SOC2 report and pen-test results.
[06:35] Ava: we'll send the security package and our standard DPA template.
[06:39] Lina: good. for evaluation, we'll define acceptance criteria: per-language intent F1 >= 0.92, average routing latency p95 < 180ms, p99 < 300ms, embedding recall@10 >= 0.85. if these are met in the pilot we move to a 3-month paid pilot with traffic ramp.
[06:58] Marcus: that gives clear cut gates. we'll instrument metrics and produce a benchmark spreadsheet with thresholds.
[07:05] Tom: deployment feasibility — if we do Private on VPC, how invasive is the install?
[07:10] Sofia: we have an appliance-style onprem bundle or a VPC private control plane; typical setup time depends on network/VPC peering and KMS setup, usually 2-3 weeks for standard infra readiness. we'll run a detailed infra checklist in the follow-up.
[07:26] Rajiv: any risks with model hallucinations for routing decisions? false positives could route incorrectly and frustrate customers.
[07:32] Marcus: we mitigate via confidence thresholds + deterministic fallbacks. also will include hand-crafted rules for critical intents and a human-in-loop option for low-confidence decisions.
[07:44] Lina: can the model support transfer learning or fine-tuning on our labeled intents?
[07:49] Marcus: full fine-tuning on big models is heavier; we recommend parameter-efficient tuning (LoRA) on a small- to mid-sized model or using retrieval-augmented prompts with a lightweight adapter. we'll include options in the bench doc.
[08:02] Elena: any compliance issues with running benchmarks on our sample data? we need an NDA addendum for sample PII.
[08:08] Ava: we'll coordinate legal but suggest de-identifying before transfer; if not possible we'll do private transfer under the DPA and a temporary NDA addendum.
[08:18] Lina: OK final recap?
[08:20] Ava: recap: Redwood runs 3-model bench on your 10k sample plus synthetic peak simulation, deliver bench results + cost estimates by 2027-12-02; AtlasCom shares data and compliance contacts by 2027-11-29; schedule infra feasibility for private deploy in early Dec. acceptance criteria spelled out (F1, latency, recall).
[08:40] Rajiv: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:44] Ava: thanks, we'll send the bench plan and security pack after this call.
[08:48] (call ends)

Notes about transcript: small mistranscriptions present (e.g., "ozone-12b" internal note), occasional speaker overlaps, filler words preserved.
